issue: Sample independence and environmental variable reporting
evidence_quote: N=76 TX, N=97-99 RX across 63 runs and 53 sessions. "Two ESP32 DevKit v1 boards, 20 cm apart, for the test bed" (line 423). "channel hopping is disabled by configuration (fixed to channel 1)" (line 427). "One board pair on a bench at 20 cm produced single-run observations: these are hardware measurements, not estimates over a population of boards, rooms, or builds, so the IQRs characterize the run and not the world" (line 471). Cluster bootstrap resamples "whole boards rather than fragments, so the two devices sharing a radio channel never count as independent samples" (line 506). Mean RSSI reported as -29.2 dBm (line 698). No explicit interference measurements reported.
location: Sections II-V, VI; Table tab:hw_benchmarks; abstract mentions 63 runs, 53 sessions
minimal_fix: Explicitly state that samples are not independent due to shared radio channel; report distance (20 cm), channel (fixed to 1), and RSSI (-29.2 dBm); note that interference was not measured; clarify that IQRs characterize single runs not population variation

evidence_quote: CYC-X25519: "219.0 ms (IQR 1.0, CI [219,219])" (Table tab:hw_benchmarks line 642). CYC-ED25519-SIGN: "1075.0 ms (IQR 1.0, CI [1075,1075])" (line 643). Registry note: "the value is a hardcoded literal in tools/recompute_paper_numbers.py (line ~158), not a parsed measurement." Statistically, CI [219,219] means all N samples produced identical millisecond-rounded values, indicating either zero variance or resolution-coarse masking of variance. Bootstrap on discretized ms data yields similarly degenerate CIs; the empirical distribution is constrained to integer ms values, so bootstrap resampling cannot produce fractional-millisecond variance estimates.
location: Table tab:hw_benchmarks rows CYC-X25519, CYC-ED25519-SIGN; Registry CYC-X25519 entry
minimal_fix: Report the degenerate CI as such with explicit note that ms-resolution may mask within-millisecond variance; if feasible, use cycle-count resolution or report the IQR alongside the CI; avoid bootstrapping discretized data without acknowledging the resolution constraint

evidence_quote: The specific phrases '5/5 sampled pairs' and '65 duplicates' do not appear in the paper or results registry. However, selection effects are present: the paper states "the corpus is also conditioned on survival: the 11 archived runs, 18 session pairs and 36 handoffs are the runs that completed, so a timing median is a median over sessions that reached the active state, not over attempts" (line 732). Delivery analysis: "Link-layer reporting overstates application-layer delivery by $\approx 8$ pp across two bidirectional ESP-NOW runs" with n=36-38 (95% Wilson $\approx [78\%, 97\%]$) (lines 700-705). The abstract states '11 capture runs, 18 session pairs, 36 handoffs' and '63 runs, 53 sessions'.
minimal_fix: Clarify that the 53-session/63-run counts represent completed sessions, not a random sample; note the survival bias in the archived capture set; if '5/5 sampled pairs' and '65 duplicates' reference an external analysis, cite the source and reconcile with paper findings

issue: 95% upper bound on 100/100 replay rejection failure rate
evidence_quote: EXP-REPLAY-REJECT: "100/100 rejected vectors" with n=100 (Registry entry, Section V.A). Registry 'RULE-OF-THREE' entry: "95% confidence upper bound on failure rate given 0 failures in 100 trials" = 3.0% (formula: 3/100*100). In context: 0 acceptance failures in 100 host-injected replay vectors. The 95% upper bound on the true replay-acceptance (failure-to-reject) rate is 3.0% (i.e., we can be 95% confident the rate is ≤ 3.0%). This does NOT mean 97% rejection confidence; it bounds the complementary error rate.
location: Registry EXP-REPLAY-REJECT entry; Registry RULE-OF-THREE entry; Section V.A
minimal_fix: Report the 95% UB as 3.0% on the replay-acceptance rate with explicit statement that this is the complementary rate; do not cite as '97% rejection confidence'; add to the paper's threat model table with proper interpretation
